claims.answer: Apple container backend on Apple-silicon macOS26 boots one lightweight Linux VM per session. Docker Desktop/Podman-machine VMs are different, shared runtime boundaries. Docker/Podman are alternative backends. Linux containers share the host kernel; gVisor or Kata may be selected if installed. README labels Podman and several runtime variants untested. Agent edits a project copy-on-write clone or ordinary copy, not a Git worktree. Real project folder is never mounted; file-name excludes omit common secrets, with content/hard-link limitations. Apple backend VM plus locked network proxy/firewall is documented separately from weaker Linux Docker/Podman isolation. Host processes running as the user can still root-exec the VM; allowed hosts can receive arbitrary TLS content, and session credentials are plaintext in runtime metadata. No hostile-code test was run.
